classification.difficultyReason: Combine several point-angle relationships and reuse intermediate values across subdivided opposite sectors.

inlines.text: Combine your knowledge of angle relationships to calculate the value of each angle.
You do not need to give reasoning.

spec.description: Three concurrent straight lines: horizontal, southwest–northeast and northwest–southeast. Plain endpoints, no vertex dot or angle arcs.
spec.mathematics: 38° lies between east and northeast; f lies in the vertically opposite west–southwest sector. Bearings describe source appearance, not additional measured givens.
spec.answerVisibility: Only 38° and f are visible; the supplied 38° answer is excluded.

spec.description: Two crossing diagonals and an extra ray slightly above east.
spec.mathematics: The left sector is 96°. The opposite sector is split into 62° above the extra ray and a below it.
spec.answerVisibility: Only 96°, 62° and a appear in the question.

answer.worked:
Vertically opposite angles are equal.
$$\begin{align*}a &= 96^\circ - 62^\circ \\ a &= 34^\circ\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Two straight diagonals cross; an extra westward ray slopes slightly upwards.
spec.mathematics: The extra ray splits the left sector into 24° above and 52° below; the opposite right sector is a.

answer.worked:
Vertically opposite angles are equal.
$$\begin{align*}a &= 24^\circ + 52^\circ \\ a &= 76^\circ\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Crossing diagonals with an additional horizontal ray to the right.
spec.mathematics: Clockwise from northwest: 108°, e, 49°, d, 72°. Both supplementary givens 108° and 72° are retained.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens and unknown labels appear.

answer.worked:
Vertically opposite angles are equal.
$$\begin{align*}d &= 108^\circ \\ e &= 72^\circ - 49^\circ \\ e &= 23^\circ\end{align*}$$

spec.description: A steep X with 55° at the top, f on both sides and g at the bottom.
spec.mathematics: Both occurrences of f are retained. Opposite sectors are equal and adjacent sectors sum to 180°.
spec.answerVisibility: Neither calculated angle is supplied on the question diagram.

answer.worked:
Vertically opposite angles are equal, so $g = 55^\circ$. Angles on a straight line sum to $180^\circ$.
$$\begin{align*}f &= 180^\circ - 55^\circ \\ f &= 125^\circ\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Two shallow crossing lines and an extra steep north-northwest ray.
spec.mathematics: Clockwise from west-northwest: 63°, x, 28°, 152°, y. The redundant supplementary pair 28° and 152° remains.
spec.answerVisibility: Calculated x and y occur only in the answer fields.

answer.worked:
Vertically opposite angles are equal.
$$\begin{align*}x &= 152^\circ - 63^\circ \\ x &= 89^\circ \\ y &= 28^\circ\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Three concurrent lines with 111° at the top, t at the bottom and four separate w labels in the remaining sectors.
spec.mathematics: t is opposite 111°; two adjacent w sectors together supplement 111°. Source proportions are schematic; no equality arcs are added.
spec.answerVisibility: 111° is the sole numerical given. All four w labels remain.

answer.worked:
Vertically opposite angles are equal, so $t = 111^\circ$. Angles on a straight line sum to $180^\circ$.
$$\begin{align*}w &= (180^\circ - 111^\circ) \div 2 \\ w &= 69^\circ \div 2 \\ w &= 34.5^\circ\end{align*}$$

spec.description: A steep and a shallow line intersect. An extra northeast ray has no southwest continuation.
spec.mathematics: Clockwise from steep northwest: 100°, c, 48°, 132°, b. Retain the 132° measurement.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the three supplied numbers and b, c appear.

answer.worked:
Vertically opposite angles are equal, so $b = 48^\circ$. Angles on a straight line sum to $180^\circ$.
$$\begin{align*}c &= 180^\circ - 100^\circ - 48^\circ \\ c &= 32^\circ\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Three intersecting straight lines: two steep diagonals and one shallow rising line.
spec.mathematics: Clockwise from northwest: 51°, a, 82°, b, 47°, c. Each unknown is vertically opposite a numerical given.

answer.worked:
Vertically opposite angles are equal.
$$\begin{align*}a &= 47^\circ \\ b &= 51^\circ \\ c &= 82^\circ\end{align*}$$

spec.description: A shallow rising line crosses a steep falling line. Additional rays point west-northwest and slightly east of south; those two extra rays are not a straight line.
spec.mathematics: Clockwise from steep northwest: 104°, 76°, l, 88°, 41°, m. All four numerical givens are retained.
spec.answerVisibility: Only supplied numerical givens and l, m are present.

answer.worked:
Angles on a straight line sum to $180^\circ$.
$$\begin{align*}l &= 180^\circ - 88^\circ - 76^\circ \\ l &= 16^\circ \\ m &= 180^\circ - 104^\circ - 41^\circ \\ m &= 35^\circ\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Two intersecting straight lines and two additional rays. An unfilled right-angle square lies between the southwest and northwest rays.
spec.mathematics: Clockwise from northwest: 37°, 53°, n, a, 21°, right angle. The entire right-side sector is n, without an east ray. The square is derived from the perpendicular northwest and southwest directions.
spec.answerVisibility: The question retains 37°, 53°, 21°, a, n and the right-angle marker only.

answer.worked:
Vertically opposite angles are equal.
$$\begin{align*}a &= 53^\circ - 21^\circ \\ a &= 32^\circ\end{align*}$$
Angles on a straight line sum to $180^\circ$.
$$\begin{align*}n &= 180^\circ - 53^\circ \\ n &= 127^\circ\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Nearly vertical and nearly horizontal straight lines cross. Additional northwest and southwest rays are separate arms, not continuations of one another.
spec.mathematics: Clockwise from north: y, 88°, 49°, 43°, 63°, x. All four numerical givens remain.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the supplied givens and x, y appear in the question.

answer.worked:
Vertically opposite angles are equal.
$$\begin{align*}x &= 88^\circ - 63^\circ \\ x &= 25^\circ\end{align*}$$
Angles on a straight line sum to $180^\circ$.
$$\begin{align*}y &= 180^\circ - 88^\circ \\ y &= 92^\circ\end{align*}$$
